question.html:
A boat is moved from land to water by rolling it across a set of cylindrical airbags.


a When fully inflated, an unloaded airbag has a diameter of 1.80 m and a length of 24.0 m. At a temperature of 15 °C, an airbag can hold 4200 mol of gas.

a.i Show that the pressure in an airbag is about 0.2 MPa. [2]

a.ii Estimate the maximum safe mass that this arrangement can hold. [3]

a.iii Identify an assumption used in this estimation. [1]

a.iv Outline the change in internal energy of the gas in the airbag. [2]

b A boat is released from rest down the slope, and it travels 14 m in 8.0 s. The mass of the boat is 4.5 × 106 kg.

b.i Calculate the average acceleration of the boat. [1]

b.ii Show that the net resistive forces on the boat are about 1.1 MN. [2]

b.iii

Draw a free-body diagram for the boat while it is moving.

[2]

c Another way to move a boat down a ramp is to place it on rigid rods. Assume that the same boat is now moved on rods of diameter 1.80 m with the same boat acceleration as before.

c.i Show that the angular displacement of a rod during the first 8.0 s of the motion is about 8 rad. [1]

c.ii Outline how two frictional forces lead to the angular acceleration of the rod. [2]

d

During the testing of the rod, it is rotated about its central axis. Point P is on the surface of the rod. At time t = 0, P is at a point 45° above the horizontal. The linear speed of P is 2.0 m s–1.

The vertical displacement x of P can be modelled with an equation x = x0 sin (ωt + φ).

d.i Calculate the angular velocity ω of P. [1]

d.ii Calculate the time it will take for P to reach the top of the circle. [1]

d.iii Determine the vertical velocity of P at t = 3.0 s. [2]
